emails.subject: European center right splits over ‘Made in Europe’
emails.excerpt: 中道右派のEU議員がEUの産業加速法案を巡る「メイド・イン・ヨーロッパ」の定義について、国
emails.subject_en: European center right splits over ‘Made in Europe’
emails.summary_en: The European People's Party, the EU Parliament's largest group, is split along national lines over how to define "Made in Europe" ahead of debate on the Industrial Accelerator Act. Spanish EPP lawmakers favor a restrictive "opt-in" system limiting procurement and subsidy access mainly to EU-27 producers, while German delegates push a broader "opt-out" model that would include the UK, Switzerland, and EEA countries by default. The outcome could significantly shape which foreign automakers and suppliers qualify for EU industrial incentives.
emails.summary_ja: EU議会最大会派である欧州人民党(EPP)は、産業加速化法(IAA)を巡り「メイド・イン・ヨーロッパ」の定義を巡って加盟国ごとに意見が分かれている。スペイン選出議員はEU27カ国の生産者を中心とした厳格な「オプトイン」方式を支持する一方、ドイツ選出議員は英国やスイス、欧州経済領域(EEA)諸国も原則含める「オプトアウト」方式を主張している。この結果次第で、公共調達や補助金へのアクセス資格を得る自動車メーカーやサプライヤーの範囲が大きく左右される可能性がある。

emails.subject_en: As the US investigates German drug prices, here’s why Europe should care
emails.summary_en: Washington is investigating whether Germany's drug-pricing system constitutes an unfair trade practice, with a formal hearing set for Tuesday. Trade experts warn that if the U.S. rules against Berlin, retaliatory tariffs could extend beyond pharmaceuticals to other German exports, with the automotive sector seen as an obvious target. Germany denies any discrimination against U.S. drugmakers and says its pricing system remains balanced and necessary for ensuring access to innovation.
emails.summary_ja: 米政府はドイツの薬価制度が不公正貿易慣行に当たるかどうかの調査を進めており、火曜日に公聴会が開かれる予定だ。貿易専門家は、米国がドイツに不利な判断を下した場合、報復関税が医薬品分野に留まらず、自動車産業など他の輸出品にも及ぶ可能性があると指摘している。ドイツ政府は米企業への差別はないとし、自国の薬価制度は技術革新への公平なアクセスを確保するための均衡の取れた仕組みだと反論している。

emails.subject_en: EU car lobby reaches position on IAA
emails.summary_en: Europe's auto industry lobby ACEA has agreed a common position on the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act, which would impose 'Buy European' rules for subsidized vehicles and batteries. However, automakers remain split on which countries should count as 'Made in Europe,' with the UK's exclusion from the scheme worrying manufacturers on both sides of the Channel given it sends 60% of its car exports to the EU.
